scope: Test-only regression for the existing Android screenshot capture/revocation/cancellation chain. No production source, tool, route, schema, migration or device change. Real Android I/O remains unverified.
delivered: FakeAdb gains allow_capture/capture_entered gates around `screencap -p`; the server fixture releases the gate on teardown so every existing Android test keeps its prior behavior.

New regression 1 (capture revocation after the frame is taken): hold screencap after the worker has entered the command, revoke the grant, release the frame; capture must fail with android_grant_revoked (or the existing authority-changed codes), publish no temp PNG under control/android-captures, insert no session_captures row, and a subsequent capture must be denied before dispatch.

New regression 2 (cancelled capture waiter): cancel the caller while screencap is held; the actual capture stays owned by the service (pending=1), later completes into exactly one session_captures row and one object reference whose bytes equal the fake device PNG, leaves no temp PNG, and the service becomes quiescent.
No assertions were weakened, no production budget/timeout was shortened, and no real device/account/model was used.

android_integration_file.notes: Real V2 SQLite, managed Python worker, isolated fake ADB; no actual device.

android_model_file.notes: Fixture compatibility after adding the capture gate; model access/input approval/revocation/scope/scroll paths.

retained_first_failures.reason: The revocation-after-capture test initially accepted only android_authority_invalid/android_grant_changed; the real repository returns android_grant_revoked. The assertion was corrected to the actual existing code, with no production change.
